a:r.a:t: Required for Recognition by Ala-tRNA Synthetase and the Synthetic Helix That Is Also Aminoacylated Specifically with Ala

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the locations of important nucleotides on tRNA using numbers, as well as the location of the G-U base pair. (a) This is a model of tRNA showing all arms and bulges. As mentioned in other models, the molecule begins with the 3' and 5' ends at the top of the structure, the amino acid arm. The 3' strand is on the right and is slightly higher than the 5' strand so that it can attach to an amino acid. It is simplest to follow the path of the molecule beginning at the 5' end and working our way around. The nucleotides themselves are all represented by black dots; however, the hydrogen bonds are still shown on the arms by blue "rungs" bridging the green backbones. Because the nucleotides are numbered from the 5' end, we will begin there. Nucleotide 1 is labeled at the very top of the 5' end. Two nucleotides down, there is the G-U bond, which is boxed in pink. There is a blue dot in between the G and U. The amino acid arm has a total of 7 hydrogen bonds (rungs) before diverging to form other arms. The 5' strand continues down and then curves left to form the D arm, beginning at nucleotide 10. The D arm extends out to the left and ends in a bulge. Nucleotide 20 is located on the bottom curve of the bulge. The bulge has nucleotides (dots) but no bonds. There are 4 hydrogen bonds on the D arm. The 5' strand curves down to form the anticodon arm, which points straight downward. It also ends in a bulge at the bottom, which has no bonds but still has nucleotides. Nucleotide 30 is on the left side of the "stem" of the anticodon arm; on the other side is nucleotide 40. There are 5 hydrogen bonds on the anticodon arm. To the right of the anticodon arm is the "extra" arm, which has nucleotides but no bonds. It is very short. Above the extra arm, at nucleotide 50, is the T psi C arm, which points out to the right. It also has a bulge at the end with no bonds, but there are nucleotides. The bulge ends at nucleotide 60, then continues with the other side of the arm, which has a total of 5 hydrogen bonds. The strand continues upward to begin the other side of the amino acid arm, which has the U of the G-U bond described earlier at nucleotide 70. The strand reaches up past where the 5' strand begins, and ends at 3', nucleotide 76. (b) An RNA minihelix with the G-U base pair. This is essentially just one "arm" of a complete tRNA. The backbone is green, with the nucleotides lined along the backbone represented by black dots. The hydrogen bonds between them are blue "rungs." Beginning from the 5' end on the left at nucleotide 1, the arm begins. Two nucleotides down, there is the G-U bond, which is in a pink box with a blue dot between G and U representing the bond. Two down, nucleotide 5 is labeled. There is a bulb at the end of the arm which contains nucleotide 10, then 13 and 66 as the bulb continues to curve around up and right. The space between 66 and 13 is bracketed and labeled "deleted nucleotides" The strand continues upward to form the other side of the arm. The G-U bond is at nucleotide 70; the strand continues up to end at nucleotide 76, the 3' end.
